w0t.text: This assistant guides you through the setup step by step. Answer the questions on each page and go on with "Next". Steps you do not need are skipped. At the end you get a check of everything and save with the button "Save" at the bottom of the page. All answers are the normal settings of the adapter – you can come back here at any time.

wizDone.label: I know ioBroker and set it up without the assistant – show all settings now
wizDone.help: All tabs appear at once. The assistant stays here and can be used at any time.

w0skip.text: All tabs are shown – choose them at the top. Do not forget "Save" at the bottom.

w0q.text: What do you want to use?

alarmEnabled.label: Alarm system
alarmEnabled.help: Monitors doors, windows and motion detectors. When armed, an open door or a movement raises an alarm: message, lamps, siren.

simEnabled.label: Presence simulation when you are away
simEnabled.help: While you are away, lamps and devices such as the TV are switched as if somebody were at home – learned from your own habits.

eveningLight.label: Evening light every evening
eveningLight.help: Every evening, also when you are at home: chosen lamps on at dusk and off at bedtime.

morningLight.label: Morning light every morning
morningLight.help: Every morning: chosen lamps on at wake-up time and off after sunrise – only while it is still dark.

w0n.text: Nothing ticked yet – tick at least one part to go on.

w0g1.text: Armed / disarmed: the alarm system is switched on / off. There are three ways of being armed: Full protection – nobody is at home, doors, windows and motion detectors are watched. Perimeter protection – you are at home, only doors and windows are watched, you can move around freely inside. Night protection – like perimeter protection, but switched on by itself at night.

w0g2.text: State: one single value in ioBroker, e.g. "kitchen window open" or "living room lamp on". You pick it with the button next to the field from the object list. Function: a group of states in ioBroker (Objects → Enumerations → Functions), e.g. "Windows" with all window contacts. If you have no such groups, simply put the devices into the tables "by hand".

wskip1.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w1t.text: The easiest way is a function (enum) of ioBroker – e.g. "Windows" with all window contacts. Everything in the function is monitored, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves. Press "Search automatically": Home Guard looks through your functions and fills in suitable ones – also lamps, presence and a door lock for the later steps. Only empty fields are filled; it takes about 15 seconds.

w1at.text: These raise an alarm in every mode – full, perimeter and night protection.

autoPerimeter.label: Use a function for doors and windows

w1bt.text: Only in full protection, i.e. when nobody is at home.

autoFull.label: Use a function for motion detectors

w1ct.text: Always active, also when disarmed. You choose whether they only send a message, also speak, or raise a full alarm.

autoFire.label: Use a function for danger detectors

hazardDefault.label: Reaction of the danger detectors of the function

w1d.text: Report only: garden gate, letter box, shed

w1dt.text: Never an alarm – just a message, e.g. "garden gate opened".

autoReport.label: Use a function for report-only sensors

w1et.text: For sensors without a function, and for the front door: add a row for the door you come in through and tick "delayed". Then opening it does not raise the alarm at once – you have the entry delay (next step) to switch the alarm system off. Tick "inverted" only if a sensor reports the wrong way round (shows "closed" when it is open). A row here overrides the same sensor from a function.

wskip2.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w2h.text: Times when arming and on alarm

w2t.text: All times in seconds. The suggestions suit most homes – press "Use suggestions" if you are unsure.

exitDelayFull.label: Exit delay full protection (s)
exitDelayFull.help: Time to leave the house after arming full protection. Suggestion: 60 s.

exitDelayPerimeter.label: Exit delay perimeter protection (s)
exitDelayPerimeter.help: You stay inside, so little time is needed. Suggestion: 0–10 s.

entryDelay.label: Entry delay (s)
entryDelay.help: Time to disarm after a "delayed" door was opened. Suggestion: 30 s.

alarmDuration.label: Alarm duration for lamps and sirens (s, 0 = until acknowledged)
alarmDuration.help: How long lamps blink and sirens sound. 0 = until somebody switches the alarm off. Suggestion: 180 s (many local rules allow 3 minutes).

openCheck.label: Open doors/windows when arming
openCheck.help: What happens when a window is still open while arming. "Warn" arms anyway and tells you which one.

armEarlyId.label: Armed at once when this contact closes (e.g. front door)
armEarlyId.help: Optional, may stay empty: the door contact of the front door. As soon as you close it behind you, the system is armed at once – no waiting for the exit delay.

w2nt.text: At night only doors and windows are monitored – you can move around inside. If you tick it, it is switched on and off by itself at the times below.

wskip3.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w3h.text: How do you switch the alarm system off?

w3t.text: Choose one or more ways. Most comfortable is a smart door lock (e.g. Nuki): unlocking the front door switches the alarm system off. Otherwise you switch it off in the panel (e.g. on the wall tablet or the phone) – a PIN makes sure only you can do that. The search in step 2 may already have filled in your lock.

lockEnabled.label: Disarm when the lock is unlocked

lockId.label: State of the lock
lockId.help: The state that shows whether the door is locked, e.g. Nuki: nuki-local.0.<id>.status.lockState

lockValues.label: Values meaning "unlocked/opened"
lockValues.help: Values that mean "unlocked". Nuki: 3, 5, 6 (the search fills them in) – a simple switch: true

pin.label: PIN (empty = no PIN)
pin.help: Empty = no PIN. With a PIN, disarming in the panel asks for it.

w3pt.text: If ioBroker already knows who is at home (e.g. through the phone in the Wi-Fi or GPS – adapters such as ping, iCloud or Life360), Home Guard can use it: when everybody has left, it can switch the alarm system on and start the simulation, and switch it off again when somebody comes home. For each person you need a state that is true while they are at home. Press "Search automatically" – it looks for a function such as "Presence".

iPersons.text: Several states of one person (e.g. GPS and Wi-Fi) get the same name in the column "Person" – the person counts as at home when one of them says so.

presenceArm.label: When nobody is at home
presenceArm.help: Suggestion: full protection – nobody is at home.

presenceDisarm.label: Disarm full protection when somebody comes home

wskip4.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w4h.text: How do you want to be told?

w4t.text: Choose how messages reach your phone – Telegram, Pushover, WhatsApp, e-mail … The matching adapter must already be installed and set up in ioBroker; the search in step 2 fills in the first one it finds. User and chat ID may stay empty – then everybody gets the message. To try it: press "Save" at the bottom first (the assistant stays open), then "Send test message".

notifyArmingFailed.label: Not armed because of open windows

notifyReport.label: Report-only sensor triggered (garden gate, letter box …)

speechId.label: State for speech (text is written)
speechId.help: Optional, may stay empty: a speaker that reads text aloud – e.g. for Alexa the state "speak" of the Echo (alexa2.0.Echo-Devices.<id>.Commands.speak).

wskip5.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w5t.text: Lamps on or blinking make the alarm visible from outside and chase intruders away; afterwards they go back as they were. Take a function with your lamps (the search may have found one) or put single lamps into the table.

w5st.text: Optional. A siren can be a smart siren, a smoke detector with a siren or a socket with a horn. Leave "Value on/off" empty when it is simply switched on and off. "Runs on": an outside siren best only in full protection, so it does not wake the neighbours when you are at home.

w5xt.text: Optional. Here you can switch anything else when something happens – one row per thing. Examples for the event "Alarm": outdoor lights or a socket on, roller shutters up, start a camera recording, the radio loud. With a second row and the event "Alarm ended" you switch it back. Other events, e.g. "Full protection armed": lock the door or roller shutters down. Value: true = on, false = off, a number for roller shutters or dimmers (e.g. 0 or 100). Scenes and scripts work too: the state of the scene, or for a script javascript.0.scriptEnabled.<name> with true.

wskip6.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w6h.text: Evening, morning and simulation – what is what?

w6e.text: Evening light: every evening, also when you are at home – the evening lamps go on at dusk and off at bedtime.

w6m.text: Morning light: on dark mornings the morning lamps go on at wake-up time and off again when it is light.

w6s.text: Presence simulation: only while you are away. It uses the same evening and morning lamps and times, and adds what makes a house look lived in: short visits to the hall or bathroom, lights out one after the other at bedtime, the TV or other devices – learned from your real evenings.

w6t.text: Here you set the times; the lamps for each part come on the next page. Every time gets a random part, so nobody can see a fixed pattern.

simCoupling.label: Runs automatically

options.label: Full protection or nobody at home

simCoupling.help: Recommended: "full protection or nobody at home" – then it also runs when you forgot to arm.

simMode.label: Planning
simMode.help: Recommended: combination. "Learned" means: Home Guard notes on normal days when you switch which lamp, and replays that – it needs a few days for it. Until then it uses random times.

simStartRandom.label: Random delay of the start up to (min)
simStartRandom.help: So the lamps do not go on at exactly the same minute every day. Suggestion: 20 min.

simEnd.label: Lights out from (HH:MM)
simEnd.help: When you usually go to bed. Suggestion: 22:30.

simEndRandom.label: Random delay of lights out up to (min)

simWeekendLater.label: Friday/Saturday later by (min)
simWeekendLater.help: On Friday and Saturday evening the lights go out this much later. Suggestion: 45 min.

simLuxId.label: Brightness sensor (optional)
simLuxId.help: Optional: an outdoor brightness sensor – on dark days the evening starts earlier, in the morning the lamps go off when it is bright.

simLuxBelow.label: Start earlier when below lux
simLuxBelow.help: Lux = brightness. Around dusk outdoor sensors show about 50–200 lux.

simWake.label: Wake-up time (HH:MM)
simWake.help: When you get up on working days. Suggestion: 06:30.

simWakeRandom.label: Random delay of wake-up up to (min)
simWakeRandom.help: So the lamps do not go on at exactly the same minute every morning. Suggestion: 20 min.

simMorningOffOffset.label: Off: minutes after sunrise
simMorningOffOffset.help: In the morning the lamps go off this long after sunrise. Suggestion: 5 min.

simMorningOffTime.label: Off at the latest at (HH:MM, empty = no)
simMorningOffTime.help: Optional: e.g. when you leave the house – then the lamps go off at the latest at this time (at the weekend later, like the wake-up time).

simMorningLuxAbove.label: Off as soon as brightness above (lux, 0 = no)
simMorningLuxAbove.help: Only with the brightness sensor above. 0 = not used.

wskip7.text: This step is not needed for what you ticked in step 1 – go on with "Next".

w7lt.text: Each lamp gets one or more roles (ticks in the table): Evening – on from dusk to bedtime (evening light and simulation). Morning – on at wake-up time (morning light and simulation). Short visits – hall or bathroom briefly, only during the simulation. Bedtime – briefly on at lights out, only during the simulation. Evening and morning lamps can simply come from a function (the search may already have found them); all others go into the table.

w7dt.text: Type "Device / scene / script": any state that is switched only while the simulation runs – TV, radio, a socket, a scene (e.g. TV on, then a channel) or a script (javascript.0.scriptEnabled.…). Best with "Learn from" its real power state, then your real evenings are replayed.

simAuto.label: Lamps through functions (evening and morning light)

w7tt.text: In the table: "Value on/off" only if the lamp needs other values than on/off (e.g. a dimmer: 80). "Learn from" only if the switching state does not show whether the lamp is really on – then choose the state that does.

simVisits.label: Short visits per evening
simVisits.help: Random short visits as long as nothing has been learned yet. 0 = only what was learned.

w8c0.text: Nothing is ticked in step 1 – Home Guard has nothing to do.

w8c1.text: ⚠ No sensors – the alarm system cannot raise an alarm. → step "Sensors"
w8c1.hidden: !(data.alarmEnabled && !(data.autoPerimeter && data.enumPerimeter) && !(data.autoFull && data.enumFull) && !(data.autoFire && data.enumFire) && !(data.sensors || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false))

w8c2.text: ⚠ No messenger – when you are away, you will not learn about an alarm. → step "Notifications"

w8c3.text: ⚠ "Disarm with the lock" is ticked, but no lock state is chosen. → step "Disarming & persons"

w8c4.text: Note: no door is "delayed" and nothing disarms by itself – opening the front door while armed raises the alarm at once. Mark the front door as "delayed" or use the lock or presence. → steps "Sensors" / "Disarming & persons"

w8c5.text: ⚠ The simulation has no lamps. → step "Lamps & devices"

w8c6.text: ⚠ The simulation should start when nobody is at home, but presence is not set up. → step "Disarming & persons"

w8c7.text: ⚠ Evening light is ticked, but no lamp has the role "Evening". → step "Lamps & devices"
w8c7.hidden: !(data.eveningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumSimLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.evening || r.type === "evening")))

w8c8.text: ⚠ Morning light is ticked, but no lamp has the role "Morning". → step "Lamps & devices"
w8c8.hidden: !(data.morningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumMorningLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.morning || r.type === "morning")))

w8ok.hidden: (!data.alarmEnabled && !data.simEnabled && !data.eveningLight && !data.morningLight) || (data.alarmEnabled && !(data.autoPerimeter && data.enumPerimeter) && !(data.autoFull && data.enumFull) && !(data.autoFire && data.enumFire) && !(data.sensors || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false)) || (data.alarmEnabled && !data.notificationManager && !(data.notify || []).some(r => r && r.instance && r.enabled !== false)) || (data.alarmEnabled && data.lockEnabled && !data.lockId) || (data.alarmEnabled && !data.lockEnabled && !(data.presenceEnabled && data.presenceDisarm) && !(data.sensors || []).some(r => r && r.delayed && r.enabled !== false)) || (data.simEnabled && !((data.simAuto && (data.enumSimLamps || data.enumMorningLamps)) || (data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false))) || (data.simEnabled && (data.simCoupling === "away" || data.simCoupling === "alarmOrAway") && !data.presenceEnabled) || (data.eveningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumSimLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.evening || r.type === "evening"))) || (data.morningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumMorningLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.morning || r.type === "morning")))

w8dt.text: Tick this box once you are done – then all other tabs with every detail setting appear. Then save.

wizDone.label: Setup finished – show all settings
wizDone.help: Shows the other tabs with every option (learning, siren modes, actions, test alarm …). The assistant stays available here.

w8save.text: Now press "Save" at the bottom of the page. Home Guard restarts with the new settings.

w8tip.text: Tip: the web component "Home Guard panel" for AURA and vis-2 shows status, buttons and the logbook.

h1.text: Home Guard – alarm system & presence simulation

i1.text: Both parts can be used on their own. Sensors, lamps and persons can be found automatically through functions (enums) or entered by hand.

i2.text: Full protection: all sensors (outer doors, windows and inside). Perimeter protection: only outer doors and windows – you are at home. Night protection: like perimeter protection, armed automatically at night. Danger detectors (smoke, water, gas) report always.

docLink.label: README: web component for AURA and vis-2, states and script commands

i1.text: All states of the chosen function are monitored. If channels or devices are in the function, their sensor states are taken. The name comes from the description of the object, otherwise from its name.

autoFull.label: Inside sensors (motion detectors) – full protection only

autoPerimeter.label: Perimeter sensors (outer doors, windows) – full, perimeter and night protection

autoFire.label: Danger detectors (smoke, water, gas) – report always, also when disarmed

hazardDefault.label: Reaction of the danger detectors of the function

autoReport.label: Report-only sensors (garden gate, letter box, shed) – a message, never an alarm

reportWhen.label: Report-only sensors report
reportWhen.help: Switch on/off at any time without a restart: state control.report

h2.text: Sensors by hand (a row overrides a sensor found through a function)

iSensors.text: "delayed": entry delay instead of an immediate alarm (the door you come in through). "inverted": the sensor reports open as false.

motionCount.label: Motion detectors: alarm only from this many different detectors
motionCount.help: 1 = every detector at once. 2 or more: a cat or a curtain alone is no alarm.

sabotageHours.label: Report sensors that have not reported for … hours (0 = off)
sabotageHours.help: e.g. empty battery or radio problem

armEarlyId.label: Armed at once when this contact closes (e.g. front door)
armEarlyId.help: Shortens the exit delay: as soon as the door is shut, the system is armed

entryDelay.label: Entry delay (s)
entryDelay.help: For sensors ticked "delayed" (e.g. front door): time to disarm after coming in

alarmDuration.label: Alarm duration for lamps and sirens (s, 0 = until acknowledged)

pinForDisarmState.label: Disarm by state only with the PIN
pinForDisarmState.help: control.mode/control.off do not disarm then – only control.pin, the panel or the lock

maxWrongPin.label: Report after so many wrong entries

pinLockMin.label: Lock the PIN entry afterwards for (min, 0 = no)

lockEnabled.label: Disarm when the lock is unlocked

lockId.label: State of the lock
lockId.help: e.g. Nuki, Danalock, Homematic or any lock with an open/closed state

lockValues.label: Values meaning "unlocked/opened"
lockValues.help: true for locks that only know open/closed – Nuki lockState: 3,5,6 (3 = unlocked, 5 = unlatched, 6 = unlocked lock ’n’ go)

i2.text: A person counts as at home when the state is true (or > 0).

iPersons.text: Several states of one person (e.g. GPS and ping) get the same name: the person counts as at home when one of them says so. States of the function can be named here too. Without a name, the object name without endings like _GPS or _Ping is used.

presenceDisarm.label: Disarm full protection when somebody comes home

notificationManager.label: Alarm also to the ioBroker notifications (notification manager)

notifyReport.label: Report-only sensor triggered (garden gate, letter box …)

notifyArmingFailed.label: Not armed because of open windows

alarmRepeatMin.label: Repeat the alarm message every minutes until acknowledged (0 = no)

speechId.label: State for speech (text is written)
speechId.help: e.g. alexa2…speak, sayit.0.tts.text or your own text state

iSirens.text: An alarm while disarmed (danger detector, panic) sounds every siren.

i3.text: e.g. lock the door when armed, roller shutters down, camera recording on alarm. Values: true, false, numbers or text.

i4.text: The test switches the ticked parts for real, marked as a test, without arming and without a real alarm. Afterwards lamps go back as before, sirens off and the actions of "Alarm ended" run. Acknowledge ends it early. Save the settings first.

confirm.title: Test alarm
confirm.text: The ticked parts are switched for real now (lamps, sirens, devices) and notifications are sent. Continue?

options.label: Full protection or nobody at home

i1.text: Learning: switching of the simulation lamps that did not come from Home Guard is stored per day. The simulation replays a whole real day with shifted times – the same weekday first, then the same kind of day (weekday/weekend). Without learned days dusk is used.

simAuto.label: Lamps through functions (evening and morning light)

iDevices.text: Type "Device / scene / script": any state that is switched only while the simulation runs – TV, radio, a socket, a scene of the scenes adapter (e.g. TV on, then a channel) or a script (javascript.0.scriptEnabled.…). With "Learn from" (e.g. the real power state of the TV) it replays the real evenings; without, it runs a few times for a random time. "When the simulation ends": automatic switches devices off and leaves lamps on (e.g. coming home). Entries in the table override the ones found through a function.

simJitter.label: Shift learned times randomly by up to ± (min)

simLearnPick.label: Choose learned day
simLearnPick.help: Weekday/weekend: any learned weekday for a weekday evening (Sun–Thu), any Friday/Saturday for the weekend. Same day of the week: a Thursday for a Thursday when at least 3 are learned.

simLearnDevicesOnly.label: Learn only switching by hand/devices (no scripts, scenes)

options.label: when it is dark (from before sunset to sunrise)

iEvening.text: Switches the evening lamps (function "evening light" or "Evening" ticked in the table) every evening, also when somebody is at home: at dusk ALL of them on (also those switched off by hand the evening before), at "lights out" ALL of them off (also those switched on by hand). Times as set under dusk. Short visits, bedtime and learned switching only run while the simulation runs – so nobody at home is surprised by the toilet light at night.

eveningLight.label: Evening light every evening, also when somebody is at home

simStartRandom.label: Random delay of the start up to (min)

simEndRandom.label: Random delay of lights out up to (min)

iMorning.text: Morning lamps (function "morning light" or "Morning" ticked in the table): on at wake-up time, off a little after sunrise – only when it is still dark. Without the morning light they run only while the simulation runs; with it every morning, also when somebody is at home.

morningLight.label: Morning light every morning, also when somebody is at home

simWakeRandom.label: Random delay of wake-up up to (min)

simMorningOffTime.label: Off at the latest at (HH:MM, empty = no)
simMorningOffTime.help: e.g. when you leave the house; later on the weekend like the wake-up time

simMorningLuxAbove.label: Off as soon as brightness above (lux, 0 = no)
simMorningLuxAbove.help: Brightness sensor from the evening section
